subject: Request: Updated subprocessor roster + DPA annex for Copperlane integration
messages:
From: Copperlane Procurement <procurement@copperlane.com>

Cc: Copperlane Legal <legal@copperlane.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: updated subprocessor roster + DPA annex for Copperlane integration

Hi Ava,

We're moving the integration window for Copperlane's payments pilot to May and the security team asked for an up-to-date subprocessor roster and the latest DPA annex that lists any subcontractors involved in telemetry, observability, or caching. Specifically we need:

- Canonical subprocessor list (names, country, purpose)
- Evidence that any telemetry vendors have EU onshore fallback / escrow plans (if applicable)
- The most recent DPA annex or addendum showing subcontractor names and data paths

I've attached our short questionnaire (subprocessor_questionnaire.xlsx) — if you can complete the high-level table and provide any attachments (evidence or export maps) that would be ideal. Can you confirm by EOD Tuesday 2026-04-06 whether you can meet that date?

Also looping in our legal team in case they have follow-ups.

Thanks,

Elena Marsh
Procurement Manager | Copperlane
procurement@copperlane.com

Attachments: subprocessor_questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessor roster + DPA annex for Copperlane integration

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the questionnaire.

Short answer: yes, we can provide the canonical roster and the DPA annex excerpt by your timeline. Attached is a compact CSV that covers our current active subprocessors and their high-level purposes; we'll follow up with the detailed evidence bundle (export maps, escrow/escrow-contact, and onshore fallback notes) by Friday 2026-04-03.

Summary (preliminary):
- Redwood core serving (self-hosted): Redwood Managed Runtime — onshore in US/EU (no change)
- Telemetry: Streamlyx (US/IE) — telemetry/metrics only; onshore fallback planned, working with Ben for evidence
- Observability: LogWave (US) — retention controls, we will attach the attestation
- CDN/cache: EdgeBridge (US/SG) — caching only, no persistent content storage; EU fallback via EdgeBridge EU region

Next steps:
1) We will complete your questionnaire and attach the DPA annex excerpt and subprocessor manifest (redwood_subprocessors_v1.csv).
2) Ben will pull the onshore-fallback matrix and attest to KMS/hsm boundaries; Marissa will include the DPA addendum export.
3) If you need an evidence call, I'm available Thu 4/2 or Fri 4/3 (I've shared a Calendly link below).

Marissa / Ben — pinging you both to own the audit pack items (KMS scope, escrow contact, and DPA annex).

Best,
Ava Chen
Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessor roster + DPA annex for Copperlane integration

Thanks — quick clarifications from security before we pull the final evidence bundle.

Onshore fallback / KMS questions:
- Streamlyx (telemetry): keys for telemetry aggregates are managed by Redwood KMS; raw payloads never stored. Streamlyx has an EU operations point and a documented fallback plan (see link below). I will attach the attestation and the contact for escrow.
- EdgeBridge (CDN): ephemeral caches only; we do not persist user content beyond TTL. For the EU fallback we use EdgeBridge EU region which keeps egress in-region; I will include the routing diagram.

One inbound question from our privacy reviewer: does Copperlane require retention of request-level logs for more than 30 days for the pilot? If you do, that changes the evidence we need to produce for exportability.

I've started a shared drive with the onshore-fallback matrix and the KMS boundary diagram: https://drive.redwood/reports/onshore-fallback-matrix

Hi Ava / Ben / Marissa — great, thanks for the quick response and the CSV.

Two quick answers:
1) For the pilot we do not require >30d retention of request-level logs; 30 days is fine.
2) We do need an escrow/escrow-contact or an onshore-safeguard owner for each telemetry/observability vendor (Streamlyx / LogWave). Can you provide the contact and the attestation PDF you mentioned?

If it's easier we can sign a short DocuSign addendum that references the DPA annex and lists the subprocessors; our legal team prefers that for procurement timelines. Could you share a Docusign template or confirm we can proceed?

Also would appreciate a 30-minute call to run through the evidence pack. I've tentatively booked Thu 4/2 16:00 PT on Ava's Calendly (if that slot still works).

Thanks,

Elena Marsh
